- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and prices are falling, model underestimates downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.6); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high and prices are trending down, model fails to recognize reversal; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day if sentiment drops below 0.4.
- Model underestimates true price drop after 10–15 days of high sentiment; add 0.5–1.0% correction to forecast for days 10–20 if sentiment >0.6.
- If sentiment is high and forecast is above 75, apply “peak decay” rule: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days to avoid overcorrection.
